simple.meaning: אֲנִי (ʼănîy) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “I.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 874 times across Genesis, Exodus, Leviticus, beginning at Genesis 6:17. Its contexts include covenant, land.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אֲנִי (H589).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: אֲנִי (ʼănîy) / H589 is traced through Genesis 6:17, Genesis 9:9, Genesis 9:12, Genesis 14:23 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.usage: I, (as for) me, mine, myself, we, × which, × who.
definitions.full: H589. ani אָ֫נִי אֲנִי, pronoun 1 singular, common I (, אֲנָא , , ) Gen 6:17 ; 9:9 , 12 + often Following a participle as its subject (to express mostly either a true present or the futurum instans [immanent future]) 18:17 אֲנִי הַמְכַסֶּה Amos I hiding from Abraham that which, etc., Judg 15:3 ; 1Sam 3:13 Jer 1:12 ; 38:14 ; 44:29 (see Dr § 135, 4 ). Appended to a verb, it expresses, in early Hebrew, a real emphasis, as Judg 8:23 בָּכֶם אֲנִי אֶמְשֹׁל לֹא I will not rule over you, 2Sam 12:28 lest I take the city, 17:15 thus and thus did Ahitophel counsel, and thus and thus אָ֫נִי יָעַצְתִּי did I counsel; but in later Hebrew It is sometimes pelonastc, Eccl 2:11 , 15 , 18 , 20 +. In response to a question, אָ֫נִי alone = I am, It is I , Gen 27:24 ; Judg 13:11 ; 1Kin 18:8 +. With הַאֲנִי הֲֶ Isa 66:9 . (Synonym אָנֹכִּי , q. v.)
